ex.en: It's a very hot day.

note: Plural ימים (yamím); two days = יומיים. The days of the week are יום + an ordinal: יום ראשון (Sunday), יום שני (Monday)… The Israeli week starts on Sunday.

ex.en: On Sunday I work from home.

note: The first working day of the Israeli week. Written יום א׳ in timetables. On Sunday = ביום ראשון; on Sundays = בימי ראשון.

ex.he: יש לי שיעור עברית ביום שני.
ex.en: I have a Hebrew lesson on Monday.

note: Written יום ב׳. On its own, שני means 'second'; before a masculine noun it is also 'two': שני ימים = two days.

ex.en: On Tuesday we're in Haifa.

note: Written יום ג׳. In speech the word יום is often dropped: נתראה בשלישי = see you on Tuesday.

ex.en: The meeting is on Wednesday at ten.

note: Written יום ד׳. Literally 'the fourth day'.

ex.he: ביום חמישי בערב אנחנו יוצאים עם חברים.
ex.en: On Thursday evening we go out with friends.

note: Written יום ה׳. For many Israelis Thursday evening is the start of the weekend.

ex.he: ביום שישי בערב אנחנו אוכלים אצל ההורים.
ex.en: On Friday evening we eat at our parents'.

note: Written יום ו׳. Many shops close early on Friday afternoon, and Friday-night dinner (ארוחת שישי) is a family tradition.

ex.en: On Saturday we go to the beach.

note: The seventh day has its own name — not יום שביעי. Feminine: שבת נעימה. Greeting: שבת שלום! On Shabbat many shops are closed and most public transport doesn't run.

ex.en: It's cold in Jerusalem in January.

note: Month names are masculine and take no ה: בינואר = in January. The Hebrew-calendar months (תשרי, ניסן…) are used mainly for holidays.

ex.en: My birthday is in February.

note: Stress on the first syllable: fébruar.

ex.en: In March we're flying to Eilat.

note: Also spelled מרס or מארס, which you often see in newspapers and official texts. All three are said merts.

ex.en: In April the weather is very pleasant.

note: Passover (פסח) usually falls in April.

ex.en: The new course starts in May.

note: Sounds like English 'my'. Don't confuse it with מי (mi) = who.

ex.en: By June it's already very hot.

note: Easy to mix up with יולי (yúli), July.

ex.en: In July the kids are on holiday.

note: Easy to mix up with יוני (yúni), June.

ex.he: אוגוסט הוא בדרך כלל החודש הכי חם.
ex.en: August is usually the hottest month.

note: Stress on the first syllable: ógust.

ex.en: In September the children go back to school.

note: The Israeli school year (שנת הלימודים) usually starts on 1 September.

ex.he: באוקטובר כבר לא כל כך חם.
ex.en: By October it's not so hot anymore.
In November I'm starting a new job.
Hanukkah is usually in December.

note: Pronounced with ts: detsémber.

ex.en: In the morning I drink coffee.

note: בבוקר = in the morning; מחר בבוקר = tomorrow morning. The plural בקרים (bkarím) is written without ו.

ex.he: בצהריים אני אוכלת עם חברים מהעבודה.
ex.en: At midday I eat with friends from work.

note: Looks like a dual (-áyim) and takes plural adjectives: צהריים טובים = good afternoon. ארוחת צהריים = lunch.

ex.en: I come home in the afternoon.

note: Written אחה״צ in timetables. In speech many people say אחרי הצהריים.

ex.en: In the evening I go to the ulpan.

note: בערב = in the evening; הערב = this evening, tonight. ערב also means 'eve': ערב חג = the eve of a holiday.

ex.en: At night the street is quiet.

note: Masculine despite the final ה: לילה טוב. Plural לילות (leilót). הלילה = tonight.

ex.en: Today is Sunday.

note: Literally 'the day'. It can also mean 'nowadays': היום הכול באינטרנט.

ex.en: I'm not working tomorrow.

note: מחר בבוקר = tomorrow morning. The day after tomorrow = מחרתיים (mokhoratáyim).

ex.en: Yesterday was a long day.

note: אתמול בלילה = last night. The day before yesterday = שלשום (shilshóm).

ex.en: I've been in Israel for a week already.

note: Same root as שבע (seven). השבוע = this week; בשבוע הבא = next week; בשבוע שעבר = last week. Plural שבועות (shavu'ót).

ex.en: This month I have a lot of work.

note: Same root as חדש (new): a Hebrew-calendar month begins with the new moon. החודש = this month; two months = חודשיים.

ex.en: This year I'm learning Hebrew.

note: Feminine, but the plural is שנים (shaním). השנה = this year; two years = שנתיים. שנה טובה! = Happy New Year (at Rosh Hashana).

ex.en: What time is it? It's eight o'clock.

note: Clock times use feminine numbers: בשעה שלוש = at three. Two hours = שעתיים. A clock or watch is שעון.

ex.en: The bus arrives in five minutes.

note: רק דקה! = just a minute! בעוד עשר דקות = in ten minutes.

ex.en: Just a moment, I'm coming!

note: On its own, רגע! = wait a sec! רק רגע = just a moment. Plural רגעים (rega'ím).

ex.en: Do you have time for a coffee?

note: Time in general. Clock time is שעה (מה השעה?), and 'a time' as an occasion is פעם (עוד פעם = one more time). בזמן = on time.

ex.en: Once more, please.

note: Feminine: פעם אחת = once, שלוש פעמים = three times, but twice = פעמיים. On its own it can mean 'once, in the past': פעם גרתי בחיפה.

ex.en: The train isn't always on time.

note: It usually comes right before the verb: אני תמיד… לא תמיד = not always.

ex.en: Sometimes I work from home.

note: Built from ל + פעמים (times).

ex.he: אני אף פעם לא אוכל בשר.
ex.en: I never eat meat.

note: It needs לא with the verb: אני אף פעם לא… — this double negative is correct Hebrew. As a one-word answer: אף פעם!

ex.he: אני הולכת לעבודה ברגל כל יום.
ex.en: I walk to work every day.

note: כל + a singular noun without ה = every: כל שבוע, כל בוקר. With ה it means 'the whole': כל היום = all day.

ex.en: I usually get up at seven.

note: Literally 'in the general way'. Abbreviated בד״כ in writing.

ex.en: The clock in the classroom doesn't work.

note: Both a clock and a wristwatch (שעון יד). שעון מעורר = alarm clock. Plural שעונים (she'oním).

ex.he: קודם שיעורי בית, אחר כך טלוויזיה.
ex.en: First homework, then TV.

note: Abbreviated אח״כ. קודם… ואחר כך… = first… and then… Unlike אחרי (after), it stands on its own, without a noun.

ex.en: I came to Israel a year ago.

note: Two meanings: before (לפני העבודה = before work) and ago (לפני שבוע = a week ago). Opposite: אחרי.

ex.en: After the lesson we have coffee.

note: Needs a noun after it: אחרי השיעור = after the lesson. On its own, 'afterwards' is אחר כך.

ex.en: Tomorrow I'm getting up early.

note: Opposite: מאוחר (late). מוקדם מדי = too early. As an adjective it agrees: ארוחה מוקדמת = an early meal.

ex.en: What's the date today?

note: Israeli dates are written day first: 3.5 = 3 May. Date of birth = תאריך לידה. A romantic date is a different word: דייט.

ex.en: I'll be there soon.

note: Literally 'a little more'. Very common on the phone.

ex.en: Jennifer is learning Hebrew at an ulpan in Haifa.

note: An intensive Hebrew course for adults, especially new immigrants (עולים חדשים); the beginners' level is אולפן א׳. The word also means a TV or recording studio.

ex.en: The classroom is on the second floor.

note: The room, the group and the school year: כיתה א׳ = first grade.

ex.en: Our teacher speaks slowly and clearly.

note: A woman teacher is spelled the same but said morá: המורה מדברת. Plural מורים / מורות.

ex.he: בכיתה שלי יש תלמידים מכל העולם.
ex.en: In my class there are students from all over the world.

note: Feminine תלמידה. A school pupil or an ulpan student; at university you're a סטודנט. Same root as ללמוד (to learn).

ex.en: Berhanu is a student at the Hebrew University.

note: Feminine סטודנטית (studéntit). Only for college and university; a schoolchild is a תלמיד.

ex.he: יש לנו הרבה שיעורי בית היום.
ex.en: We have a lot of homework today.

note: Always plural (literally 'lessons of the home'). The homework = שיעורי הבית. One lesson = שיעור (shi'úr).

ex.en: My notebook is in my bag.

note: Plural מחברות (makhbarót). Same root as חבר and לחבר (to join): pages joined together.

ex.en: Do you have a pen? — Yes, here you go.

note: Plural עטים (etím). With a pen = בעט.

ex.en: I write in pencil, not in pen.

note: Masculine with a -ות plural: עפרונות (efronót). Also spelled עפרון.

ex.en: I'm looking the word up in the dictionary.

note: Built from מילה (word). A Hebrew–English dictionary = מילון עברי-אנגלי.

ex.en: Tomorrow we have a Hebrew test.

note: בחינה is a more formal word, used for university exams and the בגרות (matriculation) exams.

ex.en: Excuse me, I have a question.

note: Same root as לשאול (to ask): לשאול שאלה = to ask a question. Plural שאלות (she'elót).

ex.en: The correct answer is B.

note: The everyday verb 'to answer' is לענות (על שאלה); the formal להשיב (to reply) shares this root, ש.ו.ב (to return). Plural תשובות (tshuvót).

ex.he: אני לומד עשר מילים חדשות כל יום.
ex.en: I learn ten new words every day.

note: Feminine, but the plural is מילים; adjectives stay feminine: מילים חדשות. Older spelling: מלה.

ex.en: This sentence is short and easy.

note: Also 'trial' and 'law': משפטים = law as a field of study. Context tells you which.

ex.en: There are twenty-two letters in Hebrew.

note: Feminine, plural אותיות (otiyót). Five letters have a final form: ך ם ן ף ץ. A letter you send is a מכתב.

ex.he: אולגה מדברת שלוש שפות: עברית, רוסית ואנגלית.
ex.en: Olga speaks three languages: Hebrew, Russian and English.

note: Also 'lip' and 'edge': שפת הים = the seashore. Plural שפות (safót).

ex.en: I'm reading a book in easy Hebrew.

note: Plural ספרים (sfarím). Same root as לספר (to tell) and מספר (number). ספר לימוד = textbook.

ex.he: יש לך דף? אני צריך לכתוב משהו.
ex.en: Do you have a sheet of paper? I need to write something down.

note: A sheet or leaf; for a page number use עמוד: בעמוד עשר = on page ten. דף הבית = a website's home page.

ex.en: The teacher is writing on the board.

note: Masculine with a -ות plural: לוחות. Also לוח שנה = calendar, לוח זמנים = timetable, schedule.

ex.en: Nour studies chemistry at university.

note: Before a name it becomes אוניברסיטת: אוניברסיטת חיפה. Plural אוניברסיטאות (universita'ót).

ex.en: My Hebrew isn't good yet.

note: Language names are feminine and end in ־ית: אנגלית, רוסית, ערבית, אמהרית, צרפתית. No את before a language: אני מדבר עברית. In Hebrew = בעברית.

ex.en: Sorry, my mistake.

note: Feminine, plural טעויות (ta'uyót). בטעות = by mistake.

ex.en: This exercise is very hard.

note: A school exercise or a physical one. Same root as רגיל (usual) and להתרגל (to get used to).

ex.he: יש לנו הפסקה של עשר דקות.
ex.en: We have a ten-minute break.

note: Same root as להפסיק (to stop). הפסקת צהריים = lunch break.

ex.en: It's a short course, only a month.

note: לעשות קורס = to take a course.

ex.en: I got a good grade on the test.

note: Israeli schools usually grade out of 100. לקבל ציון = to get a grade.

ex.en: Could I have an example, please?

note: לדוגמה = for example (like למשל). Also spelled דוגמא. Plural דוגמאות.

ex.he: אני עושה ספורט שלוש פעמים בשבוע.
ex.en: I work out three times a week.

note: לעשות ספורט = to exercise, to work out. An athlete = ספורטאי.

ex.en: The kids are playing football in the park.

note: From כדור (ball) + רגל (foot). A football match = משחק כדורגל.

ex.en: My daughter plays basketball.

note: From כדור (ball) + סל (basket). Basketball is very popular in Israel.

ex.en: In summer the kids are at the pool every day.

note: In full: בריכת שחייה (swimming pool). It can also be a pond.

ex.he: שחייה היא ספורט טוב לכל הגוף.
ex.en: Swimming is a good sport for the whole body.

note: The verb is לשחות. Also spelled שחיה. Swimsuit = בגד ים.

ex.he: אחרי ריצה אני תמיד שותה הרבה מים.
ex.en: After a run I always drink a lot of water.

note: The verb is לרוץ. לצאת לריצה = to go for a run.

ex.he: יש שיעור יוגה ביום שלישי בערב.
ex.en: There's a yoga class on Tuesday evening.

note: A yoga class = שיעור יוגה. Stress on the first syllable, as in English.

ex.he: אני הולך לחדר כושר פעמיים בשבוע.
ex.en: I go to the gym twice a week.

note: Literally 'fitness room' (כושר = fitness; בכושר = in shape). Also מכון כושר; colloquially ג׳ים.

ex.en: The movie starts at eight.

note: Plural סרטים (sratím). Also 'ribbon' or 'tape'. Subtitles = כתוביות.

ex.en: There's a new cinema in the mall.

note: ללכת לקולנוע = to go to the movies. Plural: בתי קולנוע.

ex.he: יש לנו כרטיסים להצגה ביום חמישי.
ex.en: We have tickets for a play on Thursday.

note: A theatre play or a children's show. Same root as להציג (to present, to show).

ex.en: We go to the theatre once a month.

note: Plural תיאטראות (te'atra'ót). Israel's national theatre, הבימה, is in Tel Aviv. Also spelled תאטרון.

ex.en: The concert is in the park, and entry is free.

note: Mostly for classical music; for a pop or rock show Israelis usually say הופעה.

ex.en: The show starts at ten at night.

note: Also 'appearance, looks'. Same root as להופיע (to appear, to perform).

ex.en: This is my favourite song.

note: Both 'song' and 'poem'. לשיר = to sing; a singer = זמר / זמרת.

ex.en: I listen to music on the bus.

note: Stress on the first syllable: múzika. Also spelled מוסיקה. A musician = מוזיקאי.

ex.en: There's a football match tonight.

note: Same root as לשחק (to play). Also 'acting'. A computer game = משחק מחשב.

ex.en: Do you have a hobby?

note: Same root as חביב (likeable). מה התחביבים שלך? = What are your hobbies?

ex.en: I don't have much free time.

note: פנוי = free, available, vacant (המקום פנוי? = is this seat free?). 'Free of charge' is a different word: חינם.

ex.en: Yonatan plays the guitar.

note: With instruments use לנגן ב־, not לשחק: לנגן בגיטרה.

ex.en: I'm learning to play the piano.

note: לנגן בפסנתר = to play the piano (with ב־).

ex.he: יש לי שיעור ריקוד ביום רביעי.
ex.en: I have a dance class on Wednesday.

note: The verb is לרקוד. ריקודי עם = Israeli folk dancing.

ex.en: My team is playing today.

note: A sports team or any group: קבוצת וואטסאפ = a WhatsApp group. Same root as קיבוץ (kibbutz).

ex.he: לבת שלי יש חוג ציור ביום שני.
ex.en: My daughter has an art class on Monday.

note: An organised hobby class, especially for children after school: חוג שחייה, חוג ציור. At university a חוג is a department.

ex.en: When do you have time off?

note: The everyday word for time off: אני בחופש = I'm on holiday. החופש הגדול = the long summer school holiday. A planned trip or leave from work is usually חופשה. It also means 'freedom'.
